rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-034 (illustrative figures), A-1: non-competes deter some bound workers from moves they would otherwise make; about 17% of workers had signed one and employers filed about 400 enforcement suits a year.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-034 (illustrative figures), A-5: in a material share of trainee jobs the non-compete protected the employer's recovery of the cost of general training (A-15 gives the same 0.7 for the firms' expected yield).

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-034 (illustrative figures), A-4: reshaping restraints into the forms the Act preserves (confidentiality, non-solicitation for up to 12 months, unvested deferred pay) costs many employers less than the protection it restores. The text itself names these preserved terms.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-034 (illustrative figures), A-13: employers' associations, worker groups and start-up associations can organize at a cost below their stake.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-034 (illustrative figures), A-7: some bound workers are paid less than a rival would pay them.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-034 (illustrative figures), A-2: employers stop enforcing, and workers learn that the clause is void (K4 notices).
